answer.answer:
The exact terms "Minergie" and "non-repeating panels" are not in the record; the closest terms it carries are prefabrication/off-site (PR2), reliance on precise planning (RI14), timber joinery cutting, and work on the building envelope, facade or curtain wall.

Read against those terms, the requirement is straightforward: a prefabricated timber facade is deliverable at full maturity today, but it buys its off-site advantage with precise up-front planning and logistics, and that planning burden is exactly where per-panel variation bites. Several timber joinery-cutting and assembly processes working on the envelope and facade sit at technology readiness level 9, so the fabrication capability itself is not the constraint. The pay-off recorded for moving this work off site is site safety, and that is the single cited outcome path; nothing in the record addresses envelope energy performance or certification, or panel-by-panel geometric variation, so treat those as unevidenced here rather than as solved.

**What the dependency structure requires**

Prefabrication and off-site work (PR2) depends on precise planning: prefabrication relies on precise up-front planning and logistics [1], backed by peer-reviewed evidence [1]. This is a directional dependency, not a co-occurrence, so it is a precondition rather than an observed correlate: a facade in which every panel differs multiplies the planning, sequencing and logistics load that PR2 already presupposes, and that is the first thing to resource.

The recorded benefit runs the other way: prefabrication/off-site enables improved site safety, because moving work off site improves site safety [2], also peer-reviewed [2]. That is the only enablesCapability path from PR2 in this context.

**Deployed processes that bear on it**

- census_RXT5-1, developed by Firm_199: adopted to address cost and regulation; performs assembly and timber joinery cutting; works on the structural core, the building envelope, the facade or curtain wall; at technology readiness level 9 [3]. This is the closest deployed analogue, and notably the only one of the timber envelope processes here with regulation among its adoption drivers, which is the nearest thing in the record to a standards-driven envelope job.
- census_RXT13-1, developed by Firm_181: adopted to address cost; performs assembly, material handling and timber joinery cutting; works on the structural core, the building envelope, the facade or curtain wall; at technology readiness level 9 [4]. Material handling is bundled with cutting and assembly here, which matters when every panel is a different part to track.
- census_RXT34-1, developed by Firm_130: adopted to address cost, labor and integration; performs assembly and timber joinery cutting; on the envelope, facade or curtain wall; technology readiness level 9 [5].
- census_RXH10-2, developed by Firm_102: adopted to address market; assembly and timber joinery cutting; envelope, facade or curtain wall; technology readiness level 9 [6], showing the same capability pulled by market rather than cost.

All four use timber (Material_Timber), as do further envelope-relevant records such as census_RXT1-2 by Firm_128 and census_RXT9-1 by Firm_171.

**Practical implication**

Specify the planning and logistics chain first, since PR2 will not deliver without it, and expect the geometric variation to land there rather than in the cutting cell, where readiness is already at level 9 across Firm_199, Firm_181, Firm_130 and Firm

- census_RXH10-2, adopted to address market; performs assembly, timber joinery cutting; works on the structural core, the building envelope, the facade, or curtain wall; at technology readiness level 9; developed by Firm_102.
- census_RXT13-1, adopted to address cost; performs assembly, material handling, timber joinery cutting; works on the structural core, the building envelope, the facade, or curtain wall; at technology readiness level 9; developed by Firm_181.
- census_RXM11-6, adopted to address cost, integration; performs 3d printing, concrete work, shotcrete, surface treatment; works on the structural core, the building envelope, the facade, or curtain wall, the interior fitout; at technology readiness level 7; developed by Firm_151, Firm_020.
